reuse.why: Puts the planning rule into the existing shared getScheduledAmount, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules for the approximate tolerance, and routes the API, budget template, forecast, schedule actions, posting and preview through it.

duplication.why: Removes five inline midpoint copies (schedules/app.ts x2, shared/schedules preview, forecast-schedules, schedule-template) in favour of the one helper; no new copy is added.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, already imported by both server and client; the API field is computed in the API layer from the same helper.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps, but the docs entry and api-models comment still describe 'the end furthest from zero' after step 4 changed the rule, and two release notes are left with the step-1 wording.

maintainability.why: One helper with an explicit operator parameter is easy to own; inserting amountOp before the existing positional inverse flag is fragile, and useScheduleEdit's form conversion silently inherits the planning rule because it shares the helper.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every place that resolved a schedule amount now calls getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts gains the amountOp parameter (the real variation) and an isapprox branch for the tolerance; no call site bypasses it.
